newsitem.title: USA: US warns Japan it does not want rise in trade gap.
newsitem.headline: US warns Japan it does not want rise in trade gap.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Thursday that the United States has told Japan that it does not expect to see an increase in the trade imbalance between the two countries.

"We have informed the Japanese and are going to reinforce that we do not expect Japan to export its way out of its current recession and we do not expect to see an increase in its trade surplus with the United States," Barshefsky said to reporters after a speech at the American University.

The comments were similar to remarks she made last month and comments recently made by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin. Rubin is headed to Japan, where he is expected to discuss concerns about the trade imbalance between the two countries with Japanese officials.
Barshefsky said the United States has let its views be known to the Japanese and plans to reinforce those views during Rubin's visit.
